findings.heading: From Stata / Desde Stata
findings.proposition: The English says the dplyr call is rename(new_name = old_name); the Spanish says rename(nombre_antiguo = nombre_nuevo), i.e. rename(old_name = new_name), which reverses the argument order.
findings.reader_consequence: A Spanish reader copying the pattern writes rename(old = new), which either errors with 'Column `new` doesn't exist' or renames the wrong column. The same table in the SAS section of the same Spanish file (line 234) gives the correct order, so the reader also gets two contradictory rules.

findings.heading: From Stata / Desde Stata
findings.proposition: The English gives the Stata help syntax as `help [command]`; the Spanish gives it as `[comando] help`, reversing command and keyword.
findings.reader_consequence: A Spanish reader who trusts the Stata column types `[comando] help` in Stata and gets an error instead of the help page. The Spanish SAS table (line 205) prints `help [comando]` correctly, so the two tables disagree.

findings.heading: From Stata / Desde Stata
findings.proposition: The English says user-written functions are installed with `ssc install [package]`; the Spanish says they are installed 'utilizando el [paquete] ssc install', placing the package name before the command.
findings.reader_consequence: A Spanish reader takes the installation syntax to be '[paquete] ssc install' and issues an invalid Stata command when trying to install an ado file.

findings.heading: From SAS / Desde SAS
findings.proposition: The English states that the Label statement, the Where/If record selection and the Merge statement are all used in the SAS Data Step; the Spanish drops 'in the Data Step' from all three rows (line 237 leaves the truncated fragment 'etiquetarse en el mediante la sentencia Label').
findings.reader_consequence: A Spanish reader is not told where these SAS statements belong, so the mapping from SAS to the R equivalents loses the context that these are Data Step operations; line 237 additionally reads as a broken sentence.
